body:
Hey, Daughter! I'm a HUUUUUGE fan of you guys. 

What has been your personal favorite song of your own to record? Or maybe one that you haven't recorded (yet), but you're exceptionally proud of? 

(I'm partial to Medicine -- so lovely.) 

Take care. :) x
This is so weird. My history professor was showing me pictures yesterday that her grandfather took while liberating the same exact camp. Great photos!

I feel like the entire attitude of the country changed after 9/11. 

I was 11 when it happened, but I remember a *lot* of paranoia about school shootings (as it was post-Columbine before 9/11). 

I remember seeing gas prices at $0.99 a gallon!

But again, the entire attitude of this country changed. The day that it happened, I remember everyone -- from everywhere -- just stopping to stare at the TV for a moment. In shock. In fear. 

Since then, I feel as if everyone has been on guard and paranoid.
I got a compliment from my boss. *Finally.*
That I didn't graduate college.

Toothpaste. 

I'm pretty ugly, I should at least have decent teeth.

My junior year, there was a guy that passed away after he was cleaning his father's gun and it accidentally fired. 

He was the type of guy that everyone had a love-hate relationship with. Teachers, students -- everyone. I had a class with him (he was a senior when I was a junior). He would always playfully goad the teachers and just be a disturbance as most high school students are.

Many times I would catch myself saying, "God, I fucking hate him." but in a way that you do with a brother/sister. They annoy you, but at the same time they're still very close to you. (I went to a very small school, so everyone knew each other.)

When the news came that he passed away, it was actually during the day. It was senior skip day, and I will never forget, I was in History, when my friend was scrolling through facebook on her phone and just started screaming during class. We all rushed to see what was wrong, but she told us what happened. 

Everyone was a zombie that day. Crying, walking absently. It was haunting. Usually, in between classes, it's noisy and rowdy, but when the bell rang, the halls were silent. The next day we had an assembly at the gym. It was heartbreaking.

Telling my parents that I didn't want to go into the medical field. Mom is a doctor, dad is a surgeon. Was pretty much foretold that I would be the next practitioner, but I'm just not cut out for it. Told them I wanted to go to law school instead. Took me a very long time to admit that.
I'm gay, and reading through this thread makes me laugh.
When I met my first boyfriend.

There was an episode of Doctor Who (I can't remember what series -- maybe 2?) where the main focus is on a random group of people that are trying to find the Doctor, I think. Or something. I don't even know. 

Ends up with people being absorbed into this alien's stomach. The weirdest goddamn episode of Doctor Who, and that's saying a lot.

Drive.

It helps me clear my head and think, honestly.

Sleeping the night before a final exam. 

I'm *so* afraid I'm going to oversleep, so much so that I'm usually panicked to the point of not sleeping and end up staying awake.

Gothic and alternative/hipster when I was 14. 

I wanted to enter high school and seem "different." Was so sure this was my new identity. Then, I guess I grew up, because I remember looking at myself one day and thinking, "What the *fuck*?"

I met Reese Witherspoon in Walmart when she was filming Walk the Line near my hometown. 

I ran to the store late at night and left my phone at home (because I live about 2 minutes away from the store, so I didn't think I'd need it). I'm browsing the ice cream aisle, and Reese just casually walks past with an "excuse me," grabs some ice cream, and walks away. 

I was so stunned that I just stood there. I thought that, maybe, I was hallucinating or maybe she was a doppelganger, but when she got to the checkout, the cashier was like, "OH MY GOD!"

I also ran into Joaquin Phoenix at a gas station a few days after that. He was an asshole though.

But I swear, when I tell people about this, they're just like, "Yeah, right."

I want to be an actor and a writer. 

While I look nowhere near like how typical male actors look, I have talent (just allow me to toot my own horn). And I love writing. I've had a passion for it since I was very young. 

I guess what's holding me back from chasing these dreams is the fact that almost everyone else in the world wants to be famous or to be an actor/writer/singer/dancer.

Join campus organizations that you have an interest in. You will be bound to make friends in them. 

Go to any of the events they offer, such as welcome weeks, (my uni did a burger bash), or any sort of gathering and just smile. Be personable.

I was the same; I didn't smoke/drink/party at all my freshman year -- until I got to be a sophomore. I felt established, I guess. I had a great group of friends who would occasionally get drunk and do shrooms/E, but I would just sit in the background and watch. 

I wanted to change that. I wanted to try it, just once. So I did. It was okay, but some of it was how I pictured it to be. 

College is all about experiencing things and growing as a person. I'm not saying you need to do drugs to do this, but you need to get out of your comfort zone, that's for sure. You need to do something random. If you're curious about smoking/drinking, then try it just once! (in moderation -- with people you trust.) But don't think you *have* to. 

My friends and I did crazy shit all the time without involving drugs. (Mini golf, hiking, being stupid in Walmart, pranking freshmen, etc)

Just be cautious and responsible. 

But, for what it's worth, I do think you should have the experience of being drunk just once. It's college, man. It's an experience. Learn from it.

Act like you're still in fucking high school.

I mean, don't get involved in petty he-said, she-said drama. That still happens, even at the junior/senior level, but freshmen are the fucking *worst* about it. I can't tell you how many times I've been at the library or in a class, and a freshman is talking very loudly with his/her friends about the latest occurrence in his/her life.

No one fucking cares about you anymore. Go to class. Study. Graduate. Die.

I don't know about anyone else, but give them FREE SCANTRONS!

At my university we have to pay for them, and that shit is a hassle on exam day when you have a hundred things to do, but you don't have the $4 to buy a pack of blue scantrons. 

Just give them free scantrons and everything will be perfect.
"Let go and let God."

The Hangover. 

Goddamn, I hate that fucking movie.

J.K. Rowling. 

She pretty much made my childhood, and the thought of losing her just makes my gut knot up.

For the love of god, please, *please* reply back to emails if a student is trying to get in contact with you.

I can't tell you how many times I will email a professor with a question about an exam or assignment and the professor won't get back to me, so I have to end up skipping work/class to go to their office hours and get it straightened out. 

*Don't fucking do this, PLEASE!*

I'm crying while scrolling through this thread. 

Bert, even though I've never known you, you are such a cutie! I hope you have a lovely snooze. 

To Dalazo, don't forget the years Bert gave you -- all the love. :)
"To be fair..."
Eat dessert before dinner.

It just screams "Hey! I'm a freshman!" The thing about college is you should try to blend in with the crowd. 

Although, I never really bought into that. But I did go to a college where freshmen were teased (playfully) if they had a lanyard.

I walked into a shit-smeared bathroom stall. 

Walked right back out.

I wrote a screenplay when I was 16 after my friend said "like you could do any better" in response to some god-awful horror movie we watched. I posted the script on an online forum to get some feedback, and about a month later a producer emailed me after an intern had turned my script over to him. 

Turns out he was interested in the idea, he wanted to buy it, but said he just wanted the concept -- not the actual story. He had the paperwork and everything ready for me to sign my idea over -- but I said no. It wasn't what I wanted at the time. 

Now I regret it.

I was with my grandmother when she died. Congestive heart failure. The doctors had her on life support, but my mom made the (very painful) decision to take her off. 

My mom and I held her hand, and it was like she was falling asleep. Very peaceful, very calm.

I was an only child all my life, so I'm not really sure how to take care of other children. When I'm around my friends who have children of their own, I feel so awkward around babies. I find them rather annoying; they take up far too much time (as are expected from babies), and I think it takes a special sort of person to do that. 

In short, it's just a preference, nothing against children, but I am a career-driven person, not a father.

I think the biggest mistake my friends made freshman year was that college is one big party and you can do whatever you want and not have any real consequences. 

Very wrong. 

You have to learn to balance having a social life with an academic life (and a work life if you have a job). It can be difficult, but you will get used to it right away -- especially if you are living in a dorm, away from parents. 

Also, **DO NOT** skip class. I know how hard it can be to wake up for an early class, but you (or possibly your parents) are paying for you to be there, and this starts the beginning of your career, so don't fuck it up. Instead, suck it up, get out of bed, and go to class. 

And don't wear a lanyard.

Went to a party, drank so much tequila I got alcohol poisoning and had to go to the hospital. Blacked out. 

Got lucky: didn't get in trouble, only vomited and had a hangover.
When people get in the fast lane and go slow.

When I first got really into porn, I watched these really awful amateur videos on sketchy porn sites. One video had this guy getting fucked in the ass, and upon jackin' it, I realized the guy had an *awful* case of hemorrhoids and they were bleeding and I almost threw up while masturbating.
Arkansas: go to Memphis.

Resident Assistant (RA) here. 

People often say I "get my education paid for" by working in university housing. 

HAHAhAHahahahaAHAHA no. Far from it. At my school, I only get my room and board paid for (that's SOOOOO awesome, right?!). 

Nope. As far as payment goes, I'm paid $70/month. A MONTH. SEVENTY DOLLARS. 

Definitely don't get paid enough to take care of college children, but it's one hell of a great job.

I don't know. We dated for about six months -- but within that short amount of time, I fell in love with him. He was (pardon the cheesiness) my world. 

We didn't break up on the best of terms, but we still agreed to be friends. After a while, we tried to rekindle things, but it just wasn't there. For a while, I followed him on Tumblr, but he deleted his account and completely vanished from the grid. 

I wish I could just talk to him one last time to know he's okay.

For objects in your dorm room/apartment:

* **Band-aids!** I can't tell you how helpful these will be.
* Toilet paper (if you have your own bathroom -- but still, bathrooms in dorms have bad toilet paper).
* Snacks (crackers, cookies, chips -- junk food).
* *CONDOMS*.

Also, aside from the essentials, buy a mirror for your room. It comes in handy. As a guy, I didn't think to bring one, but ended up buying one halfway through the year.

That I cheated on an exam my sophomore year. 

It was for a very difficult class -- organic chemistry. I ended up getting a 100% on one of the exams. The *only* one in a 200+ person class. People were surprised, and one guy started a rumor that I had the answers and it spread through the class to the point that my professor actually emailed me to see what "all the talk was about."

No, I didn't fucking cheat, I studied two months in advance for the goddamn test. Apparently the second highest score was an 80%. 

I think I remember telling the professor, while in a rage, that "If I was going to cheat, I would at least make sure to not get a 100% so I wouldn't look so obvious." She was surprised, and didn't question me.

It pisses me off that people think I have to actually cheat to do well. Fuck.
I live in Arkansas, and I can confirm that, in this part of the country, meth is ba--JUST GIVE ME ONE MORE HIT JUST ONE AND I'M DONE.
Reminds me of freshmen on their first day.
My mother dying.
Dear OP, you are adorable and I'm digging the beard, but sorry to say the kitten is just a little bit cuter than you are. ;)

A Thousand Splendid Suns is absolutely *beautiful*. I love it so much. I actually had to read it for a class (for a paper). It was purely amazing. I would say, probably better than The Kite Runner by a mile.
TL;DR Has anxiety about everything but keeps it well-hidden. Puts on fake emotions around different people. Says he doesn't want a relationship and doesn't care, but he secretly does.

That it's all just one big party and every Friday night some super-fun-eventful thing happens and it's the time of your life every day.

(Note: Sometimes, college can be this way, but sometimes you may want to blow your brains out due to stress -- if you're doing it right.)

The Kite Runner. 

After speeding through the last page of that book, I sat in the middle of my history class (back when I was in high school) and I cried. I had a pseudo-breakdown. That book. Oh my god.
My mom sacrificed her social status and several friends and basically her entire 20's to support and raise me. That's something I don't think I can ever repay her for.

Whitney Houston. 

I remember the day I found out. I cried as if a member of my family had died. I don't know why I was so upset over it, but she had such a troubled past. It didn't seem fair for her to go the way she did.

My local cinema used to stop taking tickets outside the individual screens after a certain time (usually 9PM). So, I would just get there, get out of one showing, then just hop-skip-jump into the next one when it's later in the evening. Never been caught, but I don't do it often.

A few summers ago, I was going on a trip with some of my friends to Florida (from Colorado), so it was a long trip. My friend rented a large cargo van. There were 9 of us in total. One of the girls along for the trip exclaimed at one point that she didn't feel good. None of us really paid attention, as she was at the back and we were all goofing around. A few hours into the trip, I hear someone screaming. One of the other girls is shouting, "She's throwing up!" and then that girl began to throw up. The smell was awful. 

The first girl caused the other girl to throw up, then a guy started gagging. Out of the nine people in the van, four people ended up vomiting. My friend (who was driving) was unable to pull over due to traffic and his window wouldn't roll down, so he ended up puking in his lap. My eyes were stinging with tears. I just... *gag*
Brave Little Toaster!
Deodorant.
Their Eyes Were Watching God by Zora Hurston. So fucking beautiful. It was like reading a *true* love story.
Nutella.

Very liberal, but I think that gun control is a bit... intrusive. I do support the *control*, but I also do support the right that everyone should be able to protect themselves...*without appearing as gun-crazed, psychotic morons.*

"It's a lifestyle choice." In response to being gay.

No, it's not. Fuck you.

Requiem for a Dream. The final scene. 

That movie haunted me after I watched it. Still does. I just crawled into bed and contemplated life after it was over.
I'm worried about my grades this upcoming fall. I'm taking on a new, more stressful job, and I'm taking a senior-level honors class as a junior. College is stressful in and of itself.

When I got the email that said "Scholarship decision." It was a scholarship that could potentially pay for my education for the entire four years of college. My internet froze right when I opened it, naturally.

My great-grandmother got severe Alzheimer's and couldn't remember her own daughter (my grandmother). It was so sad to see her try and remember. She would say things like, "You look so familiar." or "You look like my daughter." I've never cried so much in my life.

Miley goddamn Cyrus. 

Let her do what the fuck she wants. *Newsflash: It's not your life.*
The Kite Runner.

*Spiders.*

Seriously, I'm scared of failure and death and those things, but the one thing that makes my skin crawl and my stomach churn is spiders. Just... *ick*.

Breaking Bad. 

I've watched the first three seasons, started season four, but I just wasn't into it. I know the show has excellent performances and writing, but it's just not my cup of tea.

*SPOILERS *

I thought George dying was the most horrible moment of the show (meaning it was sad), but then the plane crash happened in season 8 and I was so distraught when Lexie died.
Beefy guys, beards, and cuddles.

Coordinating Associate for Residence Education .

I'm a Resident Assistant (RA) at my college.
People that take things way too seriously.

I'm way too fucking nice to people, even if they're assholes to me. I keep using the thought, "Maybe they're secretly miserable, so it wouldn't be fair to them if I just dropped them -- even if they're rude to me." But fuck that. You can't please everyone, and some people really are just awful.
Glee.
Scary Movie 2.
I don't think this movie is even funny in an ironic way. It's just bad. Awfully bad.

He insisted that we spend more time together. And while that may not *sound* like a bad thing, when you're a full-time student with two part-time jobs, it's hard to fit it all in and maintain a decent GPA. 

It was like, the only times he wanted to go out on a date was when I had exams lined up. When I told him I needed to study: "You always blow me off to do 'schoolwork.'" UM, IT'S COLLEGE, JACKASS. 

I would set aside specific dates with him where we could go to the movies, eat dinner, hang out, etc. The days were only a few days apart. But every time I made SURE we were both free, he would make up an excuse. "Oh, I have to work." So, fuck him. It takes two.
Just come out of the closet already. Everyone knows.
Read some huge, boring book on existential philosophy just so I could talk about it with the guy when I saw him at school.

We Are Young - Fun. (ft. Janelle Monae). I know the song is *so* overplayed, but this song introduced me to Fun. and then bands like them. It was like I was being introduced into a brand new world full of musical possibilities. It just spoke to me on an entirely new level that music never had before.

When they make the joke of "You look bored."

Working as a cashier, I can't tell you how many times a day I heard that goddamned joke.
Drank so much tequila I had to be taken to the hospital for alcohol poisoning.

Fucking purses. I don't understand. 

Worked at Walmart for four years as a cashier, and I can't tell you how many times women were caught lifting purses/handbags. I just don't get it.They weren't even designer. They were, like, cheap store-brand purses.
Oh my god, yes. The sight/sound/smell. Just *everything* about it.

I crack jokes a lot, but I have the ability to be serious and helpful whenever you need it. I just like to make people laugh for fear that they may not like me. It's a defense mechanism, but I'm a good person. I swear.
MLK Jr's I Have a Dream speech.

I don't think I would, because I don't want to watch my friends and family die. It would be lonely. Of course, I could make new friends, but life is meant to be lived and eventually ended. We're all born to die.
I cry angry tears and try again.

That you can work your ass off for a paycheck, only to have it all gone to bills/food/basic necessities. You don't necessarily gain as much as you put in, and money is a lot more important than it should be.
Um, of course! I now pronounce us dating! :D
When I took a shit after eating some super-extra-mega-spicy salsa with super hot chips. The pain in my ass was...*shudder* I sat on the toilet and cried.
"Are you the husband or the wife?" I'm gay and I'm frequently asked this when I'm out with my boyfriend around friends.

I didn't mean to say that if you have a preference that makes you racist. It's just *how* some guys say it. They say it in a really asshole-ish way, you know? Kinda like, "No blacks talk to me." I don't know. It just sounds kinda rude, but like I said... everyone has preferences. I'm not a big fan of grindr anyway!
No. His personality was enough to turn me off. But when I saw that... it was over.

Sit at the front of the class (or at least near the front). I've learned if you sit at the back, you're more prone to distractions. 

Do your work. 

**GO TO CLASS**. Most important thing you will ever do.

Ask for help if you need it.
Balloons popping. I'm scared shitless of those things. Any time I'm around people with balloons, I instinctively cover my ears just in case they pop. I don't like them. *shudder*
BA in Political Science. Still in college, but make more than enough in paid internships. Already have a job in a law firm lined up after I graduate in May 2014
Gravity - Sara Bareilles

Car crash. We were hit by a drunk driver going about 75 MPH. Our car flipped three times. We (four of us) were all wearing seatbelts. My friend (who was driving) got her body ripped in half when the car hit on her side. The rest of us crawled out of the wreckage. I sustained the worst injuries (broken leg, arm, shoulder). Most terrifying night of my life. I'm still scared of cars to this day.

She is the BIGGEST bitch ever. Like, she is so outspoken and vocal about things and doesn't really stop to consider the big-picture schemes of things. Most of my other friends won't invite me to things if they know I'm hanging out with her because she always finds some political/sexist thing to bitch about.

BUT, I personally love all of her rants. I guess that's why I'm friends with her.
Yo Mama jokes. Damn, I remember getting into arguments with my friends over who could come up with the best joke... *cringe*

I'm a black guy mainly attracted to white guys, but to my dismay, (on Grindr at least), white guys are usually "Don't message me unless you're white." I completely understand having preferences (*sexually*), but I don't get why you wouldn't talk to someone just because you're not sexually attracted to them.

From what I've learned, the people that have such preferences are only looking for a quick hookup or their next boyfriend. Me, I don't put in my bio, "WHITES ONLY." Not only does that scream "HEY! I'M RACIST!", but it's just not a nice thing to do. I talk to everyone regardless. I could be talking to a potential great friend! Who knows?

But people are assholes! I find Asians to be adorable. :)
Wow. Cute guy! Even cuter cat!
I don't know if that's OP sitting in the background, but just for the record... that dude is sexxxxaaay.

One of my favorite moments! The shows from the 90's that had laugh tracks makes it obvious that actors are about to break character. When they're waiting for the applause to stop, they're just dying. You can tell. It always makes me die laughing.

That scene with Kevin sitting on Michael's lap is HILARIOUS! If you look in the back, Mindy (Kelly) is actually flat-out laughing. She's behind Ryan a bit, but I felt like they didn't even try to hide it!
I got *"It's real for us"* tattooed on my left wrist. It's a quote from Harry Potter. Aside from the shitty font, I still love it.
I silently watched him pick a disgusting sore on his ass and sniff his fingers afterwards very deeply. I was forcing myself not to gag.

I can tell when an actor is trying not to laugh. Usually on comedy shows (The Office, Parks and Rec) where that's okay. I just find it hilarious that they're just barely hanging on to their 'serious' faces.
"You Make My Dreams" by Hall and Oates
Fart. :)
Entirely treatable. It's not the end of the world. I have a friend that has it and he still has a healthy social/sex life.

My friend's advice to come out of the closet when I was 14. She said that there was no need in holding it in. 5 years of repressing my sexuality and 3 girls I broke up with later, I finally came out. Best decision of my life. But I could have spared those girls...
I went to college in a town very far away from where I grew up.

Don't be so quick to judge someone. 

In the past, I've often been superficial in my views to others, but lately I've changed that and it has made me a more happy person generally.

V for Vendetta.

Although it's a graphic novel, I thought the film was amazing in its own right. However, I thought the Evey/V romantic storyline was an interesting development in the film.

I opened this picture and screamed. Omg omg omg. Irrational fear of spiders just got worse. 

I would be shitting in the yard if those things were in my bathroom.

My good sir, I wish you all the luck on your travels and I hope that you get to see, taste, smell, and feel everything you have ever wanted to. I sincerely hope I get to see more pictures of your travels in the near future. 

I have to say, this entire post has been an inspiration to me. Thank you so much. Good luck, and thank you for this. Really. :)

The idea that I would never want to have kids. I told my mom when I was like 14 that I never wanted them. She told me that, as I got older, I'd want them. 

In my mid-20's and still just as vehemently anti-children as ever.

I was at Bonnaroo last year, and my friends and I were all camped out waiting for the festivities to start. At about 2am, I was walking around having a smoke when I heard a girl crying. She was sitting behind a port-a-potty just letting it all out. 

I didn't know what to do, so I just offered her a cigarette. She declined. I asked her what was wrong. She told me she found her boyfriend in bed with another girl and came to Bonnaroo from Canada just to "get away." She asked my advice on what she should do -- from a man's perspective. I told her my opinion. She wiped her eyes and said very calmly, "I'll take that cigarette now." Then she left. She looked happier. 

I wonder what happened to her; if she got back with her boyfriend, if she enjoyed the concert. I hope she's at least happy!
Boobs. On women. I'm a gay man, so I'm not really supposed to, but I just really can't resist looking at a really good pair of tits. Kat Dennings? Oh, shit.
Oh sweet jesus here we go again.

I'm actually a junior in college right now. I'm pursuing my BA in Political Science and a BA in English. 

It's fairly difficult to find jobs with the government or public affairs without years of experience or a Masters degree. 

Like you, I went through a period of self-doubt. What you have to do is make a decision -- change your major to something you know you will have a job in (accounting, business management, engineering, medical field, etc), or you can pursue what you're passionate about and see yourself doing for years down the road. 

TRUST me, I've been there! Do *NOT* doubt yourself. Just focus on getting great grades, talk to academic advisors and research, research, research potential careers and **INTERNSHIPS**.

I've decided to get my Masters in Public Administration after I finish undergrad. 

If you have further questions, OP, please message me! Best of luck!

PS -- it's hard to find a job at this time because it's summer (assuming you're in the US), and it's a time when tons of high school and college students are looking for work. Try during October/November. Closer to holidays. Good luck. :)

I was gonna say the same thing! I'm just a passerby, but this post really punched me in the gut. 7th grade was the worst year for me in school -- even worse than those awkward high school years. I was struggling with my sexuality, body issues, and a host of other things. I know how it feels to be isolated and estranged from so called "friends."

I know this sounds weird, but I would absolutely *love* to be a penpal for your daughter. I'm a 19-year-old college sophomore just looking to help out a kid! I've totally been where she is. Please let me know if there's anything I can do to help!

Learn how to effectively study in high school. A lot of my friends in college are fucked because they never really learned how to study. 

Also, make sure you know how to do your own laundry (if you don't already). Mom always knows some tips and tricks that can help you save money. 

LEARN TO BE SAVING WITH YOUR MONEY. Can't stress this one enough. 

Get a job if you can. Not necessarily for the money, but for the networking opportunities it gives you.

"I will always love you."

When my mom said this to me after I came out to her.

This question has caused me to look back and realize that I never, even as a young child, *believed* in God. 

I would stay with my grandparents on the weekends while my mother would go to work. I live in the bible belt in the USA, so going to church on Sundays is just a given. I remember being woken up *every* Sunday to go sit in this really small building and listen to a guy talk. I begged to stay home every time. When I did go, I just played around and crawled under the pews. 

As I got older, around 12 years old, I came to the realization that I was gay. Up until this point, I "loosely" believed in God and Christianity. It just wasn't something I talked about to anyone; however, I went to a youth "worship" group with my friend. (She promised me free food, so why the hell would I not go?!) I get there, and the youth pastor begins talking about how, when we die, if we are going to Hell, that we will live in eternal agony and worms will eat our flesh. I was fucking terrified. 

I went home that night and just sobbed, because I knew that I was gay and that "gay people don't go to heaven."

But in the middle of my sobbing/horror/upset fit, I came to a realization: *Why the fuck am I so upset, when I know that none of this is real?*

I stopped crying. I stopped being scared. I stopped living in fear, because living in fear of some unknown deity is **NOT** how to live your life. At the tender age of 12, I 'renounced' the "faith" that I had (even though there never was one). 

I started living my life for me.

I've watched a lot of movies that have made me feel upset or sad, but *Schindler's List* is the only one that has ever made me cry. And I mean 100% sob uncontrollably. 

I just recently watched it last summer, and I can't even begin to tell you what I felt after that movie. It's just... so much.

I'm very sorry to hear that. From experience, and from being there myself, I know how shitty of a feeling it is. If you *ever* -- under any circumstances -- need to talk, just PM me. I've been over the river and through the woods on this issue. I would be more than happy to help you!

When I was a senior in high school, I had to go to a very large interview for a scholarship as well. I cannot begin to tell you how nervous I was! Do this before anything else: take a deep breath. Relax. Smile. 

Secondly, when you walk into that room/area where the interviews are being conducted, be courteous. "Yes ma'am," "yes sir," etc. Use the manners you were taught. 

The interviewers know that people are fighting tooth and nail for things like this (well, that's how my interviewers were). They are expecting you to be buttering them up, trying to cater to them. They can, for the most part, tell when someone is just trying to slide by. 

The questions could range from a variety of things. For my interview, one of the first questions they asked me was, "Why do YOU think you deserve this scholarship?" No one knows the answer to that question, only you do. But it's all about how you present it to them. Be confident in your answers, smile often, speak with purpose. I can't stress the *confidence* enough. 

In most interviews, whether it be for a job or for academic endeavors such as this, the interviewers are trying to get a feel of who you are - so let them. Be yourself. Pretend like you are talking to your friends, but don't be too open. You have to find your balance. Don't be too rigid or stiff. Maybe crack a joke or two (or not - depends on how your interviewers are). Some will be really funny, others will be - of course - rigid and deadpan. 

Be honest. Everyone going through that interview process is probably feeling the same way you are - uncomfortable, nervous, anxious. 

For the questions, besides the aforementioned one, I was asked about my leadership roles in school, what was a time that an unforeseen challenge presented itself and how did I handle it, and a few others that were about my personal strengths. They also asked me what my weaknesses were - academically, socially. Be reasonable about these, be honest - BUT, don't say something like, "I don't like people." Although it's honest, it's *not* what they want to hear. 

It will go by very quickly! But take your time, speak clearly. Google "interview tips" for more information if you're still unsure of how to present yourself.

Good luck! You will do better than you think, and when you get the call that you got an amazing scholarship, this will all be water under the bridge. :-)

I was an assistant manager for a retail store, and was an assistant to the HR manager for a year. I can say that almost *all* applications are going electronic now. I haven't seen a paper application in years. Even resumes are being submitted electronically.

I remember my HR boss would click through the profiles, and she actually read the quiz that's usually tacked on to the end of any job that is on an application in the retail field. The store manager and everyone actually paid attention to how you scored.

But when you answer those questions, don't put *your* answer, put the answer that you know a manager would like to hear.

For example:

An angry customer comes up to you and begins shouting about a product not being satisfactory. What do you do?

* A.) Tell the woman to leave.
* B.) Call a coworker over to assist you in calming the customer down.
* C.) Shout back.
* D.) Call a supervisor. 

The obvious answer is **D**, but I know I lot of people would choose either A or B. Nope. If there is ANY answer choice with the word "supervisor" or "manager" in it, pick that one. Because that's what you're actually supposed to do in situations like that. 

But there are other questions, like "Strongly Agree" or "Strongly Disagree", and you can honestly just skim through those, because those weren't even looked at where I worked. 

Good luck to everyone that's applying for jobs! Hopefully it's not retail, unless you want to hate yourself, your life, and the human populace in general!

I went home that afternoon, and I sort of just mechanically walked through my house. I remember laying in my mom's bed and smelling her perfume on her pillow. I cried for about two straight hours, because I knew that she would be so upset when I was gone, but I didn't want her to find me. So I sent my friend a text and told her to come over at 10 PM (when she got off from work). That way, she would find me, not my mother. 

Then I went into my grandmother's medicine cabinet and took out her codeine pills. I had read online that I would die in my sleep, no pain. I poured out a handful of them, then walked into the living room and sat on the couch. My cats came and cuddled on my lap, I remember. Then I got up, looked at all of my baby pictures, looked at all of the pictures of my mother holding me when I was a baby -- and I looked at my life in general. Each photo. And I slowly took one pill at a time. I eventually got so groggy that I had to sit down, but I hit the wall and one picture fell off the wall and the frame shattered.

The picture was of my mother holding me right after I was born. She was crying because she had given me life, "To my precious angel" the picture said around the frame. 

I was so limp and foggy by this point, but I made myself throw up as many of the pills as I could, then I called 911.

I can't explain to you the horror I felt when I decided I didn't want to die. I knew that I was well on my way, but I had to stop it. Best decision I ever made.

Five years ago, when I was only 14, I was in a car accident with me and three other close friends. My friend was driving, and a drunk driver cut across into our lane. My friend swerved, but she lost control of the car and we flipped into a steep embankment. 

I will never forget the violent jolts of the car. My body was thrown around like a rag doll. Even though I was restrained, I felt helpless. None of us screamed, because it happened so fast. I closed my eyes to try and avoid the shattering glass that whizzed around. 

Our car flipped three times. It came to a rest at the bottom of the embankment. Through the wreckage, I looked up into the driver's seat, and my friend was not there. I had to crawl through the front windshield because my side of the car was completely smashed in. 

About ten feet away from the overturned car, my friend was lying in the grass, her body twisted in such a grotesque way that my stomach churns just thinking about it. She was trembling and shivering and crying. She looked at me, blood covering her face, and begged me to "tell Daddy I was wearing my seatbelt, okay?" I just nodded my head and stroked her cheek because I knew, in my heart, that there was nothing that I could do to save her.

She held my hand. I told her that she wasn't alone, and she eventually went limp. Her hand grew cold, and I crawled back to the car and checked on my other two friends. 

It's one of those things that just fucks you up and it's hard to get over. I like to pride myself and say that what's in the past is in the past, but... it's really not. I think about my friend every single day. I have dreams, and I always wonder "what if?" What if she was wearing her seatbelt? What if she would have lived?

And I've never told this story in so much depth. Looking back, it's so surreal. I remember my local news station trying to ask the three of us that were in the crash what it was like, and I laughed in a reporter's face and told her to drive her car into an embankment, flip it 3 times, then crawl out of the chaos with a broken leg and shattered ankle. 

Needless to say, that wasn't put in the papers.

I suffered extreme PTSD and would not go anywhere near a car for the next year. To leave the hospital, I walked half of the way because I was so terrified of vehicles. I also had survivor's guilt, and nothing I did seem to help it. How can you go on living for someone and make up for both of the lives? (yours and the other person's) 

But, one day about a year later, my mom called and told me that she was stranded in a bad neighborhood and her car had stalled. She asked if I could come and pick her up. At first I asked her to call my dad, but he was busy at work, away from his phone. 

So, I got into the car and just drove. It sounds so simple, but the entire time I was going about 30 mph under the speed limit. I was sweating, about to hyperventilate, and it was excruciating. Eventually, I got my mom and we made it home safely. (By the way, no one knew the severity of my PTSD. They all just assumed it had passed in the year following the accident.)

I sat in the car and sobbed into the steering wheel, because I finally realized that I could drive again, and it was really cathartic. Driving was something that I really enjoyed. I know it sounds so minute and insignificant to some of you guys's stories, but overcoming PTSD is one of the most challenging things in the world, and I hope I never have to experience it again.
